commission: Primary official source ledger for agentic product development; capability, execution ownership, durability, availability, and interoperability.

method.sourcePolicy: Only official documentation, maintainers, and first-party release announcements; search snippets used for discovery only. Main source content inspected through web open and live Firecrawl where needed.
method.datePolicy: Publication/update dates recorded only when explicit; null means not stated. Capability facts are documentation observations, not benchmark results.
method.quotePolicy: Public claim wording paraphrased; each source kept under 200 derived words.
method.reviewPolicy: Research author cannot approve own factual or rights lane. Claims require independent fact/rights review.
method.bounds: Research scoped to named frameworks and official capability contracts; no exhaustive ecosystem coverage or vendor rankings.

sources.title: Codex SDK

claims.publicWording: The Codex SDK starts, continues, and resumes local Codex threads; the app server is the documented integration surface for custom clients handling authentication, history, approvals, and events.
The Python SDK controls the local Codex app server over JSON-RPC, requires Python 3.10+, and published builds bundle a pinned CLI runtime.
The documentation identifies the Python SDK as stable and states that codex mcp-server and the standalone codex-mcp-server binary have been removed.

limitations: Local automation is a different execution boundary from an OpenAI-managed Agents API session. Specific model access depends on the signed-in account.
sources.freshnessTrigger: Recheck on API/SDK/spec release or before implementation; do not infer account access from documentation.

sources.title: OpenAI Agents SDK

claims.publicWording: The Agents SDK provides agents, agents-as-tools/handoffs, guardrails, a tool execution loop, tracing, sessions, MCP tool calling, and human-in-the-loop mechanisms.
Sandbox agents support isolated workspaces, manifest-defined files, sandbox-client selection, and resumable sandbox sessions.
The SDK uses Responses API by default for OpenAI models; direct Responses API calls leave loop, tool dispatch, and state handling to the application.

limitations: An SDK's sessions and resumable state are not evidence that an arbitrary surrounding deployment has crash-safe durable execution.
sources.freshnessTrigger: Recheck on API/SDK/spec release or before implementation; do not infer account access from documentation.

sources.title: Agents API

claims.publicWording: The Agents API exposes an OpenAI-managed Codex harness that manages sessions, orchestration, context compaction, and recovery while the application chooses tools and execution environment.
The managed harness supports sandbox commands, skills, MCP, steering, compaction, subagent delegation, and session resumption.
The current Agents API supports data residency only in the United States and does not support Zero Data Retention; a self-hosted sandbox does not change ZDR eligibility.

limitations: The execution environment can be self-hosted while the harness and session service remain OpenAI-managed. Beta/API permissions must be checked separately.
sources.freshnessTrigger: Recheck on API/SDK/spec release or before implementation; do not infer account access from documentation.

sources.title: Agents API quickstart

claims.publicWording: Agents API requests require OpenAI-Beta: agents=v1, and the official SDKs add this header automatically.
An application API key requires api.agents.read, api.agents.write, and api.responses.write permissions; the key should remain outside the agent sandbox.

limitations: Presence in public docs does not prove a specific project's permission configuration or rollout access.

sources.title: Agent SDK overview

claims.publicWording: The Claude Agent SDK embeds Claude Code's tools, agent loop, and context management in Python or TypeScript applications running in a process the developer operates.
The SDK includes file and command tools, lifecycle hooks, specialized subagents, MCP connections, permissions, sessions, skills, and plugins.
Unless previously approved, third-party developers may not offer claude.ai login or subscription rate limits through products built with the SDK; the docs specify API-key authentication.

limitations: Operating a Claude Code process is not the same service boundary as Claude Managed Agents; authentication terms matter to resale/product architecture.
sources.freshnessTrigger: Recheck on API/SDK/spec release or before implementation; do not infer account access from documentation.

sources.title: Claude Managed Agents overview

claims.publicWording: Claude Managed Agents provides a hosted, configurable agent harness with cloud or self-hosted sandbox environments, persisted events, steering, file/command tools, web tools, MCP, and scheduled execution.
Managed Agents is beta and uses the managed-agents-2026-04-01 header; access is enabled by default for API accounts, while MCP tunnels and dreaming require research-preview access.
Stateful Managed Agents is currently ineligible for Zero Data Retention or HIPAA BAA coverage.

limitations: Claude Platform on AWS has differences in feature availability and session behavior. A self-hosted environment does not imply the hosted session service stores no data.

ADK supports Gemini and other providers, including local models, and can be containerized on customer infrastructure or deployed to Google Cloud.

The template-workflow page says graph and dynamic workflows supersede template workflows in ADK 2.0 for Python and Go.

sources.title: Graph-based agent workflows

claims.publicWording: ADK graph workflows explicitly connect functions, tools, AI agents, and human-input nodes through execution edges; the docs list Python, TypeScript, and Go v2.0.0 support.
ADK distinguishes declarative graphs, programmatic dynamic workflows, and prebuilt sequential/parallel/loop templates.
Some third-party integrations may be incompatible with graph-based workflows.

limitations: A deterministic control-flow graph does not make LLM outputs deterministic. Feature support is version- and language-specific.

SessionService manages sessions and events while MemoryService manages searchable long-term knowledge.

sources.title: Persistence

claims.publicWording: LangGraph checkpointers persist thread-scoped graph state; stores persist application-defined data outside graph state for cross-thread memory.
A graph can be compiled with a checkpointer, a store, or both.

limitations: Checkpoints, long-term memory, and external filesystem persistence are separate concerns. The old durable-execution URL currently redirects here.

sources.title: Checkpointers

claims.publicWording: LangGraph saves checkpoints at super-step boundaries and persists successful per-node writes so a failed parallel step can resume without rerunning successful sibling nodes.
Checkpoint threads enable interrupted execution, state inspection, replay/fork debugging, and fault-tolerant resumption.
LangSmith Agent Server manages checkpointing infrastructure automatically.
claims.locator: Introduction: Agent Server handles checkpointing automatically

limitations: Persisted node outputs do not guarantee exactly-once effects at external APIs; partially completed side effects still need application safeguards.
sources.freshnessTrigger: Recheck on API/SDK/spec release or before implementation; do not infer account access from documentation.

sources.title: Functional API overview

claims.publicWording: LangGraph's Functional API uses entrypoint and task primitives while sharing the same runtime as Graph API.
Resumption replays the entrypoint from its start and restores completed task/subgraph results from checkpoints rather than resuming the original line of code.
A task that started but did not finish may execute again; side effects should be idempotent and use idempotency keys or existing-result checks.

limitations: Replay depends on stable ordering of tasks and interrupts. JSON-serializable task outputs and entrypoint inputs/outputs are required.

sources.title: Deep Agents overview

claims.publicWording: Deep Agents is a harness built on LangChain primitives and the LangGraph runtime, with filesystem/context management, subagents, memory, streaming, and human-in-the-loop capabilities.
Task planning and skills are optional extensions to the default harness.
The execute shell-command tool is available only with a sandbox backend; unsupported execution/deletion tools are hidden.

limitations: Filesystem tools alone are not a security boundary. Backend selection controls where files live and whether shell execution is available.
sources.freshnessTrigger: Recheck on API/SDK/spec release or before implementation; do not infer account access from documentation.

sources.title: Managed Deep Agents

claims.publicWording: Managed Deep Agents runs the open-source Deep Agents harness on LangSmith Agent Server with threads, runs, streaming, and an MCP endpoint.
Instructions, skills, tools, middleware, memory, sandbox, identity, channels, schedules, and evals are declared in project files.
create_deep_agent returns a compiled agent operated by the developer; define_deep_agent returns a definition compiled by the managed runtime.

limitations: Do not conflate the open-source harness with the managed deployment offering; ownership of persistence, backends, and server differs.

sources.title: WorkflowAgent

claims.publicWording: ToolLoopAgent runs its loop in memory; WorkflowAgent adds workflow-backed state persistence and approvals that survive suspension.
Tool execute functions marked use step run as durable workflow steps with retries; unmarked tools remain in-memory functions.
The current docs require Workflow 5 plus ai and zod peer dependencies for @ai-sdk/workflow.
WorkflowAgent stream() is unbounded unless stopWhen is set, while generate() defaults to a maximum of 20 steps.

limitations: Automatic retries do not prove exactly-once external side effects. A workflow function and appropriate persistent runtime still need configuration.

sources.title: Build Agents on Cloudflare

claims.publicWording: Cloudflare separates communication channels, an agent harness, a durable Agents SDK runtime, and capability tools.
The runtime provides durable identity, local SQL state, real-time connections, scheduling, routing, fibers, and observability; a harness owns the model/tool loop.

limitations: The opinionated Project Think harness and the underlying Agents runtime have different responsibilities. Hosting a Durable Object does not preserve in-memory closures.
sources.freshnessTrigger: Recheck on API/SDK/spec release or before implementation; do not infer account access from documentation.

sources.title: Durable execution with fibers

claims.publicWording: runFiber registers work in SQLite and stash persists recovery state; onFiberRecovered handles work interrupted by Durable Object eviction.
startFiber durably accepts retained background work with status, retry deduplication, and cooperative cancellation.
Fibers do not replay the original closure or automatically retry application work; recovery policy belongs in onFiberRecovered. Cloudflare Workflows serves separate multi-step orchestration.

limitations: Durable acceptance is not a stored callback result. An evicted inline caller cannot receive the original result; explicit recovery logic is required.

sources.title: The 2026-07-28 Specification

claims.publicWording: MCP 2026-07-28 removes initialize/initialized and Mcp-Session-Id transport sessions; requests carry protocol version, identity, and capabilities independently.
The release introduces stateless Multi Round-Trip Requests, method/name routing headers, cacheable list results, and formal extensions.
Tasks moves into the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension; roots, sampling, logging, and legacy HTTP+SSE are deprecated with at least twelve months of support.

limitations: Application state still exists through explicit handles. Protocol release does not establish client/server version interoperability without testing.

Skill loading uses progressive disclosure: name/description discovery, full-instruction activation, then referenced resources or code during execution.

limitations: A portable instruction format does not grant tool permissions, supply runtime persistence, or prove identical behavior across compatible clients.

sources.title: Agent2Agent Protocol Specification

claims.publicWording: The current A2A specification page identifies 1.0.0 as the latest released version.
A2A defines communication between independent opaque agent systems through capability discovery, messages, tasks, artifacts, streaming, and asynchronous updates.
Peer agents can exchange work without exposing internal state, memory, or tool implementations.

limitations: A2A is an interoperability contract; the standard does not supply a durable implementation, shared permissions, or benchmarked reasoning quality.

sources.title: A2A and MCP: Detailed Comparison

claims.publicWording: MCP connects agents to tools/resources while A2A connects independent agents for task-oriented collaboration; the protocols can be used together.

limitations: A peer exposed as a simple tool does not automatically preserve richer task/session semantics. The page footer identifies Apache 2.0 licensing.

architecturalSynthesis.publicWording: Choose the owner of harness, execution environment, durable state, identity, and approvals before choosing an agent framework.
Crash recovery requires an explicit persistence and replay contract; session history, actor storage, workflow replay, and sandbox files are distinct guarantees.
A production agent needs business-level idempotency and artifact/state evaluation around externally visible effects, even when its runtime resumes automatically.
Treat skills as procedural context, MCP as capability integration, and A2A as delegated peer tasks; none replaces the runtime's authorization and persistence contract.
